correctness.rationale: Direct monomiality proof from invertibility; exact multiplicative equations; scalar-majority Z_r bound; support-s>=3 orbit constraints; stationarity of scalar squaring for invertible diagonal symmetry; exact centralizer orders for transpositions in odd/even characteristic; product-of-two-transpositions argument; Burnside normalization. The accompanying self-contained exhaustive checker independently confirms small prime fields and F_4. Limits fixed-q only; finite checks do not establish the asymptotic.

originality.rationale: The new, nonbinary q>=3 claim is the sharp large-dimension probability of nontrivial rational automorphisms, typical C_2 exceptional stabilizer, and matching first orbit-count correction. Source-premise monomial actions and general Burnside sums are acknowledged. The separately established q=2 case is excluded; no inspected primary source states or immediately supplies the sharp nonbinary probability or stabilizer distribution.
residual_risks: A general twisted-monomial orbit-asymptotic theorem expressed in different terminology may implicitly imply the leading coefficient.
All claims are for fixed q and nonsingular matrices; neither random singular matrices nor growing field orders are treated.
The binary q=2 dimension-asymptotic has accessible prior coverage and is outside the new theorem.
The asymptotic argument uses exact monomial centralizer formulas and field-dependent large-deviation constants; independent external audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: The canonical uniform-GL_n finite-field model for perfect evolution algebras has a sharp generic rigidity law with exact exponential leading coefficient and explicit typical exceptional symmetry. It yields an asymptotic isomorphism-class count at arbitrarily large dimension and addresses the dense perfect subcase of the random-automorphism question stated in the 2026 survey. This is structural and not a small arbitrary finite census; general/singular/sparse variants remain open.
